candidates.abstract: Multicomponent volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis remains challenging because competitive adsorption on sensing interfaces produces overlapping signals and obscures molecular fingerprints. Here we report a cation-directed plasmonic layered double hydroxide (LDH) platform in which secondary metal cations (Ni, Cu, or Co) modulate the d-orbital configuration of interfacial cationic sites, thereby differentiating molecule–surface interaction preferences and enabling multiplexed VOC detection. Density functional theory and time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy reveal distinct affinities, with Ni favoring π-conjugated aromatics, Cu interacting with amine- and nitro-substituted aromatics, and Co targeting carbonyl aromatics through Lewis acid–base interactions reinforced by hydrogen bonding. This cation-directed tuning enables functional group-specific signal amplification, yielding up to 10-fold enhancement in equilibrium SERS intensities compared with undoped LDHs. By integrating the three LDH variants into a multi-affinity array and coupling it with a two-stage transfer learning framework, models trained using pure-analyte spectra are adapted to previously unseen binary-to-quaternary mixtures without retraining. We achieve 100% classification accuracy with ≤6% deviation from nominal Raoult’s law-derived concentrations across eight representative aromatic VOC mixtures. This work demonstrates cation-directed electronic structure modulation in LDHs as a design principle for modulating plasmonic interfaces and achieving selective molecular recognition among representative aromatic VOCs. Volatile organic compound mixtures are difficult to analyze because competing adsorption obscures molecular fingerprints. Here, the authors tune metal cations in layered double hydroxides for selective SERS recognition and multiplexed sensing.

candidates.title: Relaxase asymmetry drives initiation of bacterial conjugation
candidates.authors: Danylo Gorenkin, Ruina Liang, Jonasz B. Patkowski, Salomé Bodet-Lefèvre, Tiago R. D. Costa, Aravindan Ilangovan
candidates.abstract: Abstract Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

candidates.title: Large-scale identification of the regulatory potential of SNPs in human neural stem cells
candidates.authors: Eline Koornstra, Eva S. van Zanten, Noud H. M. Klaassen, Lize Meert, Miguel Martinez-Ara, Mariana Pelicano de Almeida, Sander Lamballais, Mike R. Dekker, Mathias Eder, Hieab H. H. Adams, Bas van Steensel, Raymond A. Poot
candidates.abstract: Abstract GWAS have identified thousands of SNPs associated with different human phenotypes. Most SNPs are located in non-coding regions of the genome, where a small subset of causal SNPs is thought to contribute to risk by regulating transcription. However, identification of such causal variants remains challenging due to linkage disequilibrium, where blocks of SNPs are inherited together. Here, we perform a massively parallel reporter assay called SuRE in human neural stem cells to assess the transcriptional regulatory potential of 7.1 million SNPs. We identify 7,002 SNPs with regulatory potential (emVars) among the 484,057 SNPs with sufficiently high expression. These emVars are enriched in enhancers and often coincide with binding sites for transcription factors, such as ZBTB33, YY1, and ETS factors. We overlap SuRE data with eQTL data to pinpoint likely gene-regulatory variants. Additionally, combining SuRE data with GWAS for seven neuropsychiatric phenotypes identifies 187 emVars in risk loci containing 183,186 SNPs assessed by SuRE. In conclusion, our SuRE dataset provides a rich source to prioritize genetic variants that may be relevant for complex human phenotypes.

candidates.authors: Yongxin Liu, Liguo Niu, Mingzhi Liu, Renbiao Tao, Chenxin Jing, Joel Johnson, Li Xu, Yong Guan, Yubin Hu, Min Luo, Ken Ikehara, Michael Strasser, Rui Bao
candidates.abstract: Shallow marine carbonates are recognized as key agents in deep carbon cycling. However, the formation and burial of carbonates below the carbonate compensation depth still remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate carbonates from the > 7000 m water-depth Japan Trench hadal zone and find widespread authigenic calcium carbonate buried in these ultra-deep sediments. Stable and radiocarbon isotope depletions in the authigenic carbonates indicate an organic carbon (OC) source, likely primarily delivered by deep-sea landslides. Isotopic modeling suggests that subduction of these OC-derived carbonates can impart negative δ13C signatures to fluids released in the NE Japan subduction zone. The OC-derived carbonate flux in the Japan Trench is estimated to reach ~ 28.6 Tg C Myr–1. We propose that earthquake-driven organic matter influx into the hadal zone may have facilitated sustained carbonate production. Thus, OC-derived authigenic carbonates in hadal trenches represent an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth. Earthquake-driven organic matter influx into hadal zones facilitates sustained organic carbon-derived carbonate production. The formation of these authigenic carbonates represents both an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

candidates.title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
candidates.authors: Jialin Li, Zicong Jiang, Jingling Yang, Tianle Cai, Jing Wang, Dongjing Zhou, Yang Yun, Mingshan Zhu, Jing Zheng
candidates.abstract: Catalytic ozone decomposition has proven to be the most efficient and cost-effective method for mitigating O3 pollution, while further advancement in this field is hindered by the unsatisfactory humidity resistance and poor long-term stability of current catalysts. This study employs water transport confinement and electronegativity modulation in confined nanospaces of catalyst to address these challenges. We design a hydrophilic dual-space confined CoO mesocrystal (mesoCoO-P5) featuring hierarchically organized 0D nanocavities and 2D interlayers. The densely networked hydrogen bonds on the hydrophilic confined surface restrict water mobility, thereby preventing catalyst poisoning from water accumulation. Meanwhile, the presence of electronegative hydroxyl groups on catalyst promotes the conversion of peroxide intermediates into O2. The mesoCoO-P5 catalyst achieves stable ozone decomposition for over 24 hours under 70% relative humidity. High activity is maintained at −5oC and an ultrahigh space velocity of 4000 L·g−1 h−1, while accelerated ozone decomposition performance is demonstrated in a 3 m3 indoor room and under dust-coexisting conditions. This work establishes confinement engineering as a novel paradigm for enhancing anti-poisoning properties in the design of robust environmental catalysts. Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions.

candidates.title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root
candidates.authors: Tom Denyer, Pavel Solansky, Arvid Herrmann, Francesco de Martino, Efthymia Symeonidi, Valentin Brösamle, Marja C. P. Timmermans
candidates.abstract: Abstract Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

candidates.abstract: The hippocampus serves as a hub of cognition, and its subfields differ in their susceptibility to aging and neurological disorders. Here, we established normative references for hippocampal and subfield volumes using 3D T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans from 34,789 healthy individuals (range from 4 to 85 years), revealing varied peak ages (27.4-40.1 years) across subfields. We then mapped the hippocampus and its subfields across various neurological disorders (mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, cerebral small vessel disease, and multiple sclerosis) by deriving personalized deviation (centile) scores from these references in 3,521 patients. These centile scores captured disease-specific hippocampal abnormalities, supported disease classification, and were associated with cognitive performance, longitudinal cognitive outcomes, and disease progression across disorders. Finally, a personalized hippocampal health report was developed to facilitate clinical translation. These findings demonstrate the value of hippocampal and subfield normative references for personalized diagnosis, cognitive assessment, and prognostic evaluation across neurological diseases. This study establishes age-specific reference ranges for hippocampal subfields and shows that personalized deviations from these norms can distinguish neurological disorders and help assess cognition and disease progression.

candidates.abstract: Thermal management in highly integrated chips and wearable devices is increasingly constrained by non-uniform heat flux distributions that resist both precise sensing and efficient energy recovery at the nanoscale. The transverse thermoelectric effect (TTE), in which the temperature gradient and the resulting thermoelectric voltage are spatially decoupled, offers a geometry-compatible route to on-chip heat sensing and harvesting, but prior implementations have required strong external magnetic fields or sub-liquid-nitrogen temperatures. Here we show a submicron graphene device that exhibits a transverse thermoelectric response at room temperature and zero magnetic field, which we term the ballistic transverse thermoelectric effect (BTTE). Enabled by asymmetric scattering of ballistic carriers, the device achieves a transverse Seebeck coefficient of 27.9 μV K−1, and a transverse thermoelectric power factor of ~35.8 μW cm−1 K−2. The transverse voltage retains its polarity upon reversal of the temperature gradient, enabling nanoscale heat-flow sensing and energy harvesting under spatially varying thermal conditions. The transverse thermoelectric effect (TTE) holds promise for on-chip heat sensing and harvesting, but it is usually limited by the need for magnetic fields or cryogenic temperatures. Here, the authors report the observation of TTE (with transverse Seebeck coefficient up to 27.9 μV K−1) in asymmetric graphene nanodevices operating at room temperature and zero magnetic field.

candidates.abstract: Electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) for wastewater treatment is often limited by its reliance on high-conductivity media, restricting applications such as nitrate-contaminated groundwater remediation. Here we show that a copper-modified electrochemical nickel membrane reactor (Cu/eNMR) can remove nitrate from deionized water. For water containing 50 mg/L NO3−-N, Cu/eNMR achieves 90.5% nitrate removal at 5 mA/cm2 within 3 h, with an energy consumption of 0.139 kWh/g-N, compared with 12.8% removal and 8.6 kWh/g-N for a conventional reactor using the same cathode. Mechanistic analysis reveals that nitrate hydrogenation is enabled by direct electron transfer to the reaction chamber, coupled with directional K+ migration that maintains charge neutrality, while interfacial charge-transfer resistance governs electron-flow direction. The membrane configuration also suppresses anodic side reactions, including active chlorine formation, chlorinated by-products, organic polymerization and metal-induced anode deactivation. Solar-powered treatment of real groundwater further demonstrates practical applicability, while life-cycle analysis indicates reduced greenhouse-gas emissions compared with conventional electrochemical and biological treatments. This architecture broadens the feasible application of ECH to low-conductivity water treatment. Electrochemical hydrogenation is promising for water remediation yet limited by high energy use in poorly conductive media. Here, the authors report a copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for energy-efficient nitrate removal from low-conductivity water.

However, achieving high-performance wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) remains a significant challenge because of their high interface trap density (Dit) and large threshold voltage (VTH) variation. Here we show the distinct polarization switching mechanisms of AlScN FeFETs based on an ultrathin indium gallium oxide (IGO) channel with three different structures. FeFETs with a metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) structure show high interface quality with low Dit and a stable VTH, achieving a large memory window (MW) of up to 20.6 V and a high endurance of 106. The stable 6-bit operation of our devices with 64 distinct states shows the feasibility of multilevel storage applications. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of the FeFET in neuromorphic networks, with a high recognition accuracy of 93.02%. AlScN field-effect transistors for non-volatile memory are limited by high interface trap density and threshold voltage instability. Wang et al. demonstrate annealing-free AlScN ferroelectric transistors with low interface trap density and stable threshold voltage, enabling a large memory window and robust 6-bit operation.

candidates.abstract: Abstract An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBV p ) in healthy adults ( n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBV p ) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ 40&42 , GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α–XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte–IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

candidates.abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. As these processes blur the boundary between wildland fuels and the built environment, living with fire is becoming a reality for a growing number of communities. Under business-as-usual conditions with no adaptation, structural losses are projected to nearly triple nationwide, with 133,200–449,100 buildings expected to be damaged or destroyed by mid-century. The West remains the epicenter of losses. There, 30% of census tracts projected to face the highest fire risk intersect with socioeconomic hardship, potentially placing the greatest losses in some of the most vulnerable communities. Coupled with an eastward expansion of risk already underway, these findings signal a narrowing window for targeted intervention. Fire increasingly threatens homes across the United States as climate change and development reshape risk. Without adaptation, structural losses could nearly triple by mid-century, with the greatest losses in the West and risk expanding eastward.

candidates.authors: Chang Liu, Jianan Chen, Gang Chen, Peisheng Wang, Peng Cao, Yifan Nie, Jin Zou, Xiuyan Li, Mingli Qin, Xuanhui Qu
candidates.abstract: Oxygen is traditionally detrimental to ductility in titanium alloys. Recent advances have reframed oxygen as a design tool for forming beneficial microstructures and enhancing performance. Yet, its role has been mostly limited to the α phase in dual-phase α-β titanium alloys. Introducing sufficient oxygen into β when both phases coexist may unlock beneficial motifs and improve performance. We present that strategic oxygen partitioning across coexisting α and β phases enables substantial oxygen in β and triggers a β → O' phase transformation via atomic rearrangements. This O' phase acts as a precursor for stress-induced martensitic transformation (O'→α") during deformation, activating synergistic transformation-induced and twinning-induced plasticity. The resulting α-β-O' titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V-0.39O) achieves an ultimate tensile strength of 1200 ± 30 MPa, ductility of 23.5 ± 1.5%, and a strength-and-strain product of 28.2 GPa·%. Our work establishes a general principle for strategically tuning oxygen in titanium alloy design and demonstrates potential for recycling oxygen-contaminated titanium waste. This study utilizes oxygen-rich Ti powders for additive manufacturing and establishes a method for strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases in high-performance titanium alloy design which strengthens Ti-alloys with oxygen, rather than embrittling them.

candidates.title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
candidates.authors: Diego A. Esquivel, Angie Penagos, Anderson Feijó, Maria João Ramos Pereira
candidates.abstract: Abstract Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes.

candidates.authors: Oscar WH Wong, Suisha Liang, Yuzhou Chen, Ye Peng, Qi Su, Chun Pan Cheung, Yuqi Wu, Whitney Tang, Stephy WS Ho, Holly HL Lo, Angela MW Lam, Sandra SM Chan, Patrick WL Leung, Flora YM Mo, Caroline KS Shea, Carol SW Ho, Ting Fan Leung, Francis KL Chan, Siew C. Ng, Hein M. Tun
candidates.abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition. Although the gut microbiome has been implicated in ASD, prior studies have insufficiently addressed clinical heterogeneity. Here, we perform shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from 720 children with ASD (median age 8 years, 87% male) and 151 matched controls. Children with ASD are stratified into three severity groups using 14 symptom subscales covering core features and co-occurring psychopathologies. Microbiome composition is significantly associated with clinical severity and individual symptoms; however, the proportion of microbiome variance explained by these clinical factors is modest (R 2 = 0.0017–0.0065). Children with higher severity show reduced abundance of Lachnospiraceae bacterium AM48_27BH, a short-chain fatty acid producer, together with reduced predicted capacity of GABA-related modules (GABA synthesis II, putrescine degradation and GHB degradation), while NAD+ salvage pathways show trend-level associations with severity. Sensory atypicalities have the largest number of associated microbial markers and show trend-level links to reduced predicted capacity for degradation of excitatory neurotransmitters. These findings demonstrate that gut microbiome composition varies across the ASD severity spectrum and that different symptom domains differ in their relevance to microbiome alterations. Whether alterations in GABAergic metabolism contribute to clinical severity, and whether microbial features are preferentially linked to sensory atypicalities, remain to be tested in mechanistic and longitudinal studies.

This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Genetic disruption of Pf MD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of Pf MD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these Pf MD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in Pf MD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that Pf MD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, Pf MD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes Pf MD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Here, we combine evolution-informed design (EVdesign) with rational design to engineer improved poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) hydrolases (PETases). Designs derived from multiple PETases reveal strong parent-dependent differences in success and performance, with Thermobifida fusca Tf Cut2 emerging as the most design-amenable scaffold. Increasing sequence diversification reduces the number of active enzymes but broadens performance variance, enabling discovery of high-performing outliers. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in Tf Cut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Overall, we experimentally test 603 designs from eight parent PETases. More than 400 variants containing 12-68 substitutions were able to depolymerize PET, nearly all outperforming their parent enzymes, and many approach benchmark LCC-ICCG performance in partial conversion assays. These results establish EVdesign as a robust strategy for generating diverse, high-activity enzymes.

candidates.title: Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
candidates.authors: Heng-Yu Ruan, Xin Zhang, Zhi-Wei Zhai, Jia-Mei Yu, Xuefeng Bai, Jian-Rong Li
candidates.abstract: Purification of hexafluoroethane (C2F6) from ternary mixtures containing hydrofluorocarbons (C2H2F4 and C2HF5) using conventional routes is energy-intensive. Here, we report C2F6 purification through shape-selective molecular sieving in a molecular-trap metal-organic framework enabled by isoreticular pore-geometry tuning. Starting from PCP-FDCA, we constructed BUT-313 by a minimal O-to-S substitution in the dicarboxylate linker. This single-atom edit transforms the original rectangular channel into an hourglass-like bottlenecked pore with a narrowed constriction of 4.2 Å. As a result, BUT-313 strongly suppresses the uptake of the more symmetric C2F6 while still adsorbing the anisotropic fluorocarbons C2H2F4 and C2HF5. At 298 K and 100 kPa, BUT-313 exhibits the highest uptake ratios of 7.7 for C2H2F4/C2F6 and 6.0 for C2HF5/C2F6, together with a record-high C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0. In ternary breakthrough experiments, BUT-313 delivers >99.98% C2F6 with a productivity of 184.5 L/kg, while retaining its performance over multiple cycles and after scale-up to the 10 g level. By replacing oxygen with sulfur in a MOF linker, researchers reshaped rectangular pores into hourglass bottlenecks, switching separation from thermodynamic to geometry-driven sieving. BUT-313 achieves C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0 and purifies >99.98% C2F6 from ternary mixtures, with stable performance after 10-g scale-up and cycling.

candidates.title: Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots
candidates.authors: Huifang Song, Angel Baudon, Matthias Freund, Marek Randuch, Aleš Pěnčík, Ondřej Novák, Zhaohui He, Kerstin Kaufmann, Nan Li, Matthew Gilliham, Jiří Friml, Rainer Hedrich, Shouguang Huang
candidates.abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Auxin signaling acts as a central regulatory hub in this process, yet the mechanisms that dynamically tune auxin signaling in real time remain unknown. Here, we use the light-gated, Ca2+-permeable Channelrhodopsin 2 variant XXM2.0 to optogenetically impose defined Ca2+ signatures on Arabidopsis root cells. Repetitive light activation triggers cytosolic Ca2+ signals that in turn suppress membrane depolarization and Ca2+ transients triggered by exogenous auxin. Moreover, prolonged optogenetic Ca2+ stimulation affects auxin-responsive transcriptional reprogramming. As phenotypic output, reversible inhibition of root growth by suppressing cell division and elongation is observed. We further identify a candidate CaM7–CNGC14 module that likely mediates Ca2+-dependent gating of responsiveness to exogenous auxin as well as Ca2+-dependent root growth inhibition. Our study thus introduces a synthetic biology approach to decompose calcium–auxin crosstalk in plant cells, and demonstrates that optogenetically imposed cytosolic Ca2+ signals act as dynamic regulators of auxin susceptibility in roots. Under environmental stress, plants must balance growth and arrest. Here, the authors use optogenetics to show that Ca2+ acts as a stop signal that modulates exogenous auxin responses and root growth via a candidate CaM7–CNGC14 module.

candidates.title: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
candidates.authors: Feng Liu, Fuqi Yao, Hong Sun, Chengbao Wu, Bing Liu, Yihang Tong, Chunhong Dai, Han Wu, Ruowen Zhang, Dedong Yin, Xiaowei Xiang, Tianhang Feng, Liye Liu, Peng Zhang, Nan Wu, Yanli Jiao, Zaizai Dong, Lingqian Chang
candidates.abstract: Androgenetic alopecia affects over 1.5 billion individuals, causing progressive hair loss with psychological and quality-of-life burdens. Current pharmacological treatment for androgenetic alopecia faces challenges due to systemic side effects from oral medications or limited efficacy of topical applications. Herein we develop a comb-shaped bioelectronic system, named “Detangle”, for efficient androgenetic alopecia treatment during daily hair combing. This system features electronic teeth embedded with height-differentiated electrodes and integrated drug-loading modules, which generate an enhanced electric field penetrating up to ~9 times deeper into hair follicle regions than conventional external application. We show that the localized electric field synchronizes electro-stimulating hair follicles, and electro-delivering vascular endothelial growth factor A encoding plasmid and steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 targeting siRNA into follicular cells to promote angiogenesis and suppress androgen synthesis. Through the synergistic regulation of cellular metabolism, the system significantly increases hair restoration efficacy in an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, improving the outcome from ~70% to nearly 100% within one month compared to conventional topical minoxidil treatment. The Detangle system proves safe and effective for deep tissue delivery in dermatology. Here authors introduce a comb‑shaped bioelectronic device that uses enhanced electric fields for electrostimulation and deep acid delivery for androgenetic alopecia treatment. In mouse models, they show that this safe, non‑invasive approach achieves nearly 100% hair regrowth within one month.

candidates.title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
candidates.authors: Changyue Zhao, Zhicheng Ji
candidates.abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

candidates.title: Chromosomal location reprograms genetic circuit function
candidates.authors: Lorea Alejaldre, Jesús Miró-Bueno, Angeles Hueso-Gil, Lewis Grozinger, Huseyin Tas, Sina Geißler, Ángel Goñi-Moreno
candidates.abstract: Chromosomal position is known to influence gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains largely unexplored. Here, we expand the scope of positional effects by showing that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning. Using bacteria as a living chassis, we engineer 219 spatially distinct genetic circuits of four different types—three regulatory cascade circuits and a toggle switch. We show that spatial positioning can not only modulate circuit performance but also switch circuits between different dynamics, giving rise to new operational modes as circuit complexity increases. A mathematical model parameterized from experimental data predicts three distinct functional regimes for the toggle switch and links chromosomal position to switch stability through noise. This reprogramming is fundamentally mediated by changes in gene expression noise, moving beyond simple Boolean (on/off) or analog (more/less) interpretations of gene regulation and towards stochastic and probabilistic principles for cellular computation. Chromosomal position influences gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains unexplored. Here the authors reposition genetic circuits within a bacterial genome and show that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning.

candidates.title: Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
candidates.authors: Di Wang, Bo Zhao, Xiaoran Zhang, Hui Liang, Hao Chen, Bingchao Yang, Xiaobing Liu, Quan Li, Yanming Ma
candidates.abstract: The transformation from graphite to diamond is a paradigmatic pressure-induced structural phase transition in solids with fundamental insights in condensed matter physics, geoscience, and materials science. However, the atomistic pathway remains a subject of longstanding debate due to the challenge in observing the ultrafast nucleation process. To overcome the limitations of traditional high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) experiments, which rely on post-mortem analyses that obscure early-stage dynamics, here we combine metadynamics simulations with HPHT synthesis using dimensionally distinct carbon precursors to elucidate the microscopic nucleation and growth mechanisms. Our simulations reveal scale-dependent transformation pathways in which fluctuations in interlayer bonding precede the formation of persistent sp3-bonded diamond-like nuclei. Experimentally, by exploiting the radial confinement of multi-walled carbon nanotubes to suppress growth kinetics, we successfully capture the elusive nucleation stage, identifying 2–6 nm diamond nuclei. Using highly oriented pyrolytic graphite, we demonstrate a temperature-driven shift from interlayer to intralayer growth, which subsequently governs the genesis of twin boundaries and hexagonal diamond lamellae during final grain coalescence. These findings not only reconcile disparate theoretical models regarding the kinetic pathway but also establish a robust, precursor-mediated framework for the microstructural design of high-performance diamond materials. The study uncovers a scale-dependent graphite to-diamond pathway, showing that interlayer bonding fluctuations precede nucleation and precursor confinement captures nanoscale nuclei and regulates growth, providing a unified view of this transition.

candidates.authors: Raman van Wee, Sara De Bragança, Eva M. Martín-Cuevas, Ángel Rivera-Calzada, Sean A. candidates.abstract: Abstract Repair of double-strand breaks via non-homologous end joining requires the synapsis of DNA ends. APLF is emerging as an important repair factor, capable of forming synaptic bridges in the presence of the Ku70/Ku80 heterodimer. However, only a single one-to-one interaction between Ku70/Ku80 and APLF has been reported to date, which is fundamentally insufficient for synapsis. Moreover, it remains unclear how APLF-mediated bridging of Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers is prevented in the absence of double-strand breaks. Using a combination of single-molecule techniques, including Mass Photometry, Atomic Force Microscopy, and Magnetic and Optical Tweezers, we demonstrate that APLF-mediated synapsis requires threading of at least two Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers per DNA end. We show that this requirement stems from the need for a simultaneous interaction of two poly(ADP-ribose) binding Zinc Fingers in APLF with threaded poly(ADP-ribosyl)ated Ku70/Ku80s on a single DNA. We further provide evidence that long non-coding RNA NIHCOLE cooperatively binds up to four Ku70/Ku80, consistent with a synapsis efficiency enhancement mechanism based on the bridging of two Kus70Ku80s bound on both sides of the break. Our results propose a model for the physiological significance of Ku70/Ku80 threading and a regulatory mechanism based on multivalency that restricts APLF-mediated bridging to DNA-bound Ku70/Ku80.

candidates.abstract: Abstract Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders.

candidates.title: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
candidates.authors: Yang Li, Yang Yu, Yiming Kang, Zongtian Yin, Shihan Ma, Yuxuan Wei, Qing Li, Xinjun Sheng, Dario Farina, Xiangyang Zhu
candidates.abstract: Abstract Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. During isolated finger flexion, tissue movement directions estimated from dynamic ultrasound delineate compartment contours, which are mapped into a 3D MRI reference to generate volumetric compartment masks. Using these masks as constraints, tractography reconstructs 3D fiber trajectories and yields compartment-specific architectural measurements. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces.

candidates.authors: Anton Yang, Jianwei Ai, Costas Arkolakis
candidates.abstract: Abstract We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Combining plant output data with geospatial data, such as ambient air pollutants, nighttime lights, and temperature, we train machine learning models to predict plant locations and output. We identify about 88% (94%) of plants missing from the training sample within a 1 km (5 km) radius and achieve R 2 above 0.8 for output prediction at a 1 km grid and at the plant level, as well as both regional and time series validations. We use the model trained on Chinese steel data to reliably detect the location and measure the total annual output of steel plants in South Korea and Iran. Our approach can be adapted to other industries and regions, and used by policymakers and researchers to track and measure industrial activity in near real time.

candidates.title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
candidates.authors: Lichen Bai, Li Fu, Jian Song, Jianing Zhou, Houyu Ma, Yong Mao, Yafang Guo, Yue Liu, Jian Wang
candidates.abstract: Tailoring elastic modulus of alloys or composites is typically achieved through composite or solute effects. In this work, we demonstrate that simultaneous enhancement of elastic modulus and hardness in Au50Ag20Cu30 alloys can be realized via elastic strain engineering, enabled by three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures (3D-CDSs) which was self-organized through spinodal decomposition. Microstructural characterization and nanoindentation testing confirm the alternating hydrostatic compressive or expansion strains associated with the coherent dual-phase structure. This strain modulation leads to significant enhancements in elastic modulus (by 27%) and hardness (by 37%) compared to solid solution phase. These results are consistent with theoretical predictions and molecular dynamics simulations. Our study presents a rational and effective strategy to simultaneously tailor high elastic modulus and mechanical strength through 3D elastic strain engineering. By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy.

candidates.title: A critical role for the ER membrane complex (EMC) in lipid homeostasis
candidates.authors: Érika De Carvalho, Abdulbasit Amin, Richard Little, Keily Fonseca Silva, Catarina J. Gaspar, Marina Badenes, Emma Burbridge, Ruy M. candidates.abstract: Abstract The ER membrane complex (EMC) facilitates insertion of integral membrane proteins into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lipid bilayer. Recent years have seen significant progress in understanding the structural aspects of EMC, but the identity of EMC-client proteins and EMC’s functional roles throughout evolution remain less well understood. Here we delete the essential EMC3 subunit in the liver and adipose tissues of mice and examine the impact of EMC loss-of-function in a range of metabolic and lipid homeostasis models. The absence of EMC3 in either the liver or adipose tissues results in defective storage of triglycerides and perturbations in lipid droplet (LD) homeostasis. EMC-deficient adipose tissues have reduced ability to mediate fat storage in mice on a high-fat diet and are unable to support non-shivering thermogenesis. Proteomic analyses of EMC3-deficient tissues show reduced levels of FITM2, a key regulator of LD biogenesis and ER homeostasis, identifying FITM2 as an EMC client. Deletion of EMC3 in the Drosophila fat body reveals similar defects in LD homeostasis, which can be rescued by a FITM2 mutant whose biogenesis was EMC-independent. Together, our results indicate that the EMC plays a key evolutionarily conserved role in the biogenesis of machinery maintaining triglyceride storage in metazoans.

candidates.authors: Yuhao Geng, Xude Yu, Jianhong Xu, Jing Yu, Atul N. Parikh
candidates.abstract: Abstract Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. By integrating spatiotemporal imaging, bulk kinetics, and mathematical modeling, we quantitatively link enzymatic activity to dynamic molecular redistributions across phases, revealing how reaction-driven fluxes regulate enzymatic reactions within biphasic droplets and demonstrating the noise buffering capability of the coacervate phase.

candidates.title: Endocannabinoid-mediated rescue of somatosensory cortex activity, plasticity and related behaviors following an early-life concussion in male mice
candidates.authors: Jérôme BADAUT, Lea HIPPAUF, Mathilde MALINCONI, Brenda P. NOARBE, Andre OBENAUS, Christophe J. DUBOIS
candidates.abstract: Abstract Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.

candidates.title: First-Principles Calculation of Coherence Length and Penetration Depth Based on Density Functional Theory for Superconductors
candidates.authors: Mitsuaki Kawamura, Takuya Nomoto, Niklas Witt, Ryotaro Arita
candidates.abstract: We develop a first-principles framework for evaluating the fundamental length scales of superconductivity, namely the coherence length $ξ_0$ and the magnetic penetration depth $λ_\mathrm{L}$, within superconducting density functional theory (SCDFT). By incorporating finite-momentum Cooper pairs, we formulate a microscopic scheme that enables a consistent and parameter-free determination of $ξ_0$, $λ_\mathrm{L}$, and the superconducting transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ on the same theoretical footing. Applying the method to representative elemental superconductors, the A15 compound V$_3$Si, and H$_3$S under high pressure, we obtain results in good agreement with available experimental and reproduce the type-I/type-II classification across all materials studied. The unified access to $ξ_0$ and $λ_\mathrm{L}$ further allows us to construct the Uemura plot entirely from first principles, showing that higher-$T_\mathrm{c}$ systems are characterized by the simultaneous realization of strong pairing and large phase stiffness. Our results establish a predictive first-principles route to superconducting length scales and provide a microscopic interpretation of empirical correlations in superconductivity.

candidates.title: Dimensional Reduction Is Supersymmetric at Three Loops
candidates.authors: Mrigankamauli Chakraborty, Sven-Olaf Moch
candidates.abstract: We resolve the long-standing claim that regularization by dimensional reduction (DR) fails to preserve supersymmetry in supersymmetric Yang–Mills (SYM) theories at three loops. Earlier results reported a mismatch between the Yukawa and ghost-gluon β functions in N = 2 SYM, suggesting a breakdown of supersymmetry. We show that this discrepancy does not originate from DR itself but from subtleties in the treatment of the Clifford algebra. A corrected three-loop calculation restores full supersymmetric behavior, and we demonstrate that the same issue would first affect N = 4 SYM only at five loops, consistent with existing four-loop results. Our findings confirm that DR preserves supersymmetry for N = 1 , 2 , and 4 SYM through the loop orders examined.

candidates.title: Chiral Entangled-State Generation through Dissipative Quantum Dynamics
candidates.authors: Huixia Gao, Konghao Sun, Yiwen Han, Lei Xiao, Dengke Qu, Kunkun Wang, Xiang Zhan, Wei Yi, Peng Xue
candidates.abstract: Dissipation, though often detrimental to quantum entanglement, can be manipulated for the preparation of entangled states, wherein ingeniously designed quantum jump processes drive the system toward the desired steady state. Here we venture beyond this paradigm, and demonstrate a new type of entanglement generation in dissipative quantum dynamics. Combining driven-dissipative steady-state engineering and adiabatic passage, we propose a general protocol where the final entangled state depends on the chirality of the evolution path in the parameter space, a scheme that is further extendable to multipartite entanglement. By simulating the Liouvillian dynamics through the quantum Langevin equation for a pair of photons, we experimentally confirm the noise-resistant chiral preparation of various entangled states with high fidelity and concurrence. Our work establishes parametric chiral dynamics as a scalable and robust tool for controllable entanglement generation, paving the way for its applications in quantum information.

candidates.title: Building Far-from-Equilibrium Effective Field Theories Using Shift Symmetries
candidates.authors: Xin An, Robbe Brants, Michal P. Heller, Yi Yin
candidates.abstract: Contemporary understanding of thermalization in quantum field theory stems largely from understanding properties of transient excitations of equilibria. These nonhydrodynamic excitations are known to structurally differ between weakly and strongly coupled quantum field theories with no known results at intermediate values of the interaction strength. We demonstrate that all the known behaviors of transient excitations can be understood as a consequence of different realizations of a symmetry principle, the shift symmetry, applied at the level of the far-from-equilibrium generalization of the hydrodynamic effective action that we explicitly construct. Our approach naturally includes the effects of stochastic fluctuations outside the hydrodynamic regime and allows to explicitly construct hybrid models interpolating between weak- and strong-coupling behavior. We study properties of one such model motivated by thermalization in nuclear collisions in light of the QCD running coupling.

candidates.title: Finite-Size Scaling Theory of Rényi Thermal Entropy for Second-Order, First-Order, and Weakly First-Order Quantum Phase Transitions
candidates.authors: Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, Zheng Yan
candidates.abstract: Establishing the nature of a quantum phase transition in finite-size simulations—whether continuous, first order, or weakly first order—is a fundamental challenge in quantum many-body computation. The weakly first-order transition is particularly elusive: its anomalously large correlation length invariably mimics a continuous critical point at accessible system sizes, and no unified finite-size scaling theory has existed to distinguish these scenarios under realistic computational constraints. In this work, we address this problem by introducing a finite-size scaling framework based on the Rényi thermal entropy (RTE) and its derivative (DRTE). We derive the finite-size scaling forms for the RTE and DRTE at continuous, first-order, and weakly first-order quantum phase transitions and show that the DRTE isolates the universal contribution of the free energy and strengthens the characteristics of various phase transitions in finite sizes. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate accurate data collapse and extraction of critical exponents at ( 2 + 1 )-dimensional O ( N ) critical points. Most importantly, the DRTE provides a definitive signature of weakly first-order transitions at visitable sizes—a zero crossing and a double-peak structure—which we observe in the debated deconfined quantum criticality candidates such as the J − Q and SU(8) J 1 − J 2 models. Our approach offers a general, order-parameter-agnostic, and numerically efficient diagnostic tool, resolving long-standing ambiguities between continuous and weakly first-order scenarios in the finite-size simulations.

candidates.abstract: Heat transport in solids is usually described in a phenomenological way via Fourier's law. However, at small time and length scales in low thermal conductivity materials, a microscopic description is needed. This is traditionally done by invoking the phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE), which has been successful in describing transport in high thermal conductivity materials. Recently, a generalization of the BTE, the Wigner Transport Equation, was developed to be able to microscopically describe transport in low thermal conductivity materials by taking into account not only phonon scattering processes but also phonon tunneling processes, so-called coherences. We present a Python package that solves the Wigner Transport Equation (WTE) in spatial and temporal Fourier space for arbitrary source terms, thereby enabling the study of heat transport at small space and time scales. This allows one to compute both static and dynamic thermal conductivities from bulk to nanoscale. Beyond that, it can be used to study the response of phonon systems in materials to arbitrary heat sources.

candidates.abstract: We present a closed theory, exact in the $N\to\infty$ limit, of the equilibrium spin correlations of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model evolving with Glauber dynamics, above and at the transition temperature $T_c$. The derivation uses a dynamic cavity approach: in the evolution equation for the selected spin the other spins are represented by a fluctuating field. The influence of the selected spin on this field is included at the linear response level; it is given as a sum of the spin's past flips weighted by the correlations of the unperturbed fluctuating field. The self-consistency condition relates the time-dependent correlations of the selected spin and those of the fluctuating field. The theory predicts a $(T-T_c)^{-2}$ divergence of the relaxation time upon approaching the transition and an $At^{-1/2}$ decay of spin correlations at $T_c$. A numerical solution of the theory gives the amplitude, $A=0.964\pm 0.007$. The theoretical predictions are in excellent agreement with Glauber dynamics computer simulations.

candidates.abstract: We study two restrictions of Baxter's symmetric twenty-vertex model on the triangular lattice, in which the three classes of vertices allowed by the ice rule carry the weights $a$, $b$ and $c$: chiral ice, in which only the twelve chiral vertices are allowed, and the model that excludes only the two alternating vertices. We show that neither model belongs to any of the known exactly solvable families of the twenty-vertex model, and we characterise chiral ice as the ice model in which every vertex has exactly one through line, a property that imposes a parity constraint along every closed lattice line. We compute the residual entropies of both models with transfer matrices on cylinders of up to twelve vertices in circumference, extrapolated with the finite-size correction predicted by conformal invariance, which we adapt to the triangular geometry and verify at two exactly solved points. The number of upward arrows crossing the cylinder is conserved, and the cost of changing it shows that both models are critical, with the long-distance behaviour of a free massless field. Chiral ice is the extreme point of a region of the phase diagram in which ordering had been suggested; along two paths through that region we find the same critical behaviour at every point, with no feature at the proposed boundary of the region. Along Baxter's exactly solved curve we obtain the corresponding exponents in closed form.

candidates.abstract: Long-range interactions in machine-learning interatomic potentials are commonly treated by coupling learned sources through either a prescribed electrostatic kernel or a learned but configuration-independent one. Whether such a kernel suffices depends on the underlying screened interaction. We address this question by using Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn how latent source fields, built from the descriptors of a local backbone (here MACE), interact across the simulation cell. For a synthetic ionic system with tunable screening, a prescribed Coulomb kernel underestimates the long-wavelength charge fluctuations by 43% under strong screening, whereas the FNO reproduces them within 3% and recovers 95-99% of the variance of the residual left by the local backbone. A linear FNO, which learns a configuration-independent kernel, performs equally well in the homogeneous case. Under inhomogeneous screening, rearranging the remote medium modulates the coupling between distant ions, a dependence that no configuration-independent kernel can represent. Among the models tested, only the nonlinear FNO responds to this modulation, and its force errors are 27-41% lower than those of configuration-independent models. In first-principles benchmarks of liquid water, lithium lanthanum zirconate, and Au2/MgO(001), MACE-FNO is comparable to a prescribed-kernel model for the bulk systems and more accurate for the interface. It further captures the reversal of the Au2 wetting preference induced by remote Al dopants, with deviations below 5 meV per cell from density functional theory. These results indicate that a configuration-dependent kernel, as learned by FNOs, becomes necessary once the screening medium varies, even though the energy remains quadratic in the charges for a fixed medium.

candidates.abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) instabilities in two-dimensional materials are governed by strongly anharmonic soft phonons, whose dynamical behavior remains poorly understood beyond the statically renormalized vibrations. Here, using monolayer 1H-NbSe2, we investigate how frequency-dependent three- and four-phonon interactions reshape phonon spectral functions and influence electronic excitations. We find that three-phonon interactions induce substantial dynamical softening of CDW modes, increasing the estimated transition temperature relative to static self-consistent phonon theory. Four-phonon interactions further promote such dynamical softening and enhance spectral broadening, producing non-Lorentzian lineshapes that challenge the quasiparticle picture. Incorporating dynamically renormalized phonon frequencies and electron-phonon coupling into Fan-Migdal electron self-energy calculations reveals enhanced electronic kinks, satellite features, and momentum-dependent quasiparticle decoherence, driven by the strong momentum dependence of the electron-phonon coupling matrix elements. These findings establish dynamical anharmonicity as a critical link between soft-mode lattice fluctuations and electronic spectral signatures, providing insights into coupled lattice-electron dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.

candidates.abstract: The ubiquitous power-law relaxation emerges from complex mechanical systems with a vast number of interacting exponential responses. Here we demonstrate that power-law responses satisfy a maximum entropy criterion, regulating the individual contributions under partial knowledge. This leads to a prediction that frequency range of validity decreases with power-law exponent, a property which is confirmed for some biological materials. The close relation with the fractional standard linear solid also leads to an incorporation of the equally ubiquitous stretched exponential behavior.

candidates.abstract: The Korringa factor $K(α)$ in the nuclear magnetic resonance studies is a widely used measure of electron-correlation effects in metals and is conventionally interpreted using the non-correlated value $K(α)$ = 1. In Dirac-fermion systems, however, the non-correlated reference value depends on the electronic density of states (DOS) and differs from that of conventional metals. Here, we theoretically investigate the non-correlated Korringa factor $K^*(α)$ in a Dirac nodal-line (DNL) system with finite nodal-line dispersion using a DOS-based approach. We show that $K^*(α)$ exhibits an intrinsic temperature dependence, continuously evolving from the Dirac-fermion value of 1.71 at high temperatures to the metallic value of 1 at low temperatures. The crossover temperature is found to be proportional to the nodal-line dispersion width, identified as the characteristic energy scale governing the non-correlated Korringa factor in DNL systems. We further demonstrate that Landau quantization generates singular DOS structures that strongly enhance $K^*(α)$, producing pronounced peaks even in the absence of electron correlations. In addition, $K^*(α)$ exhibits two distinct types of magnetic oscillations arising from intra-level and inter-level contributions. The latter originates from the overlap of singular points belonging to positive and negative quantum-number Landau subbands at the Fermi level and represents a unique consequence of the finite energy dispersion of a DNL. These results provide a quantitative reference for interpreting NMR experiments in DNL materials and for identifying genuine correlation effects beyond DOS-induced contributions.

candidates.abstract: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

candidates.abstract: We show that a microscopic model of twisted MoTe$_2$ with screened Coulomb interactions produces topological superconductivity. Using the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) on infinite cylinders, we find that the narrow Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ has Cooper pair correlations that strengthen with cylinder circumference, consistent with two dimensional superconductivity. The superconductor has chiral $f$-wave pairing around the valley center, and its topology produces chiral Majorana edge modes and non-Abelian vortex cores. At zero displacement field, the superconductor spans fillings $-0.78\lesssimν\lesssim-0.72$, close to the experimental range, and extends in a dome to finite displacement field. We then predict how its stiffness evolves with the filling and the tunable displacement field. The interplay with screening length is also examined. Nearby, we find a fractional Chern insulator, a topological charge density wave, a metal, and a charge-ordered state. The last is a candidate for the reentrant integer Hall regime in experiments. These results establish a route from repulsive interactions in microscopic models of moiré materials to chiral topological uperconductors with chiral Majorana edge modes.

We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath. candidates.abstract: Intrinsic electron localization in amorphous silica (a-SiO2) contributes to charge trapping and defect generation in silica-based electronic materials - a phenomenon that degrades logic-device performance but can be exploited for memory applications. However, the structural distribution of one- and two-electron traps remains incompletely characterized, largely because the disordered covalent network of a-SiO2 spans a vast configurational space. To address this, we perform statistical sampling to select a representative 200-model subset of defect-free bulk a-SiO2 structures from a structurally converged parent set of 2512 models, generated via classical melt-quench molecular dynamics simulations. We then characterize the intrinsic one- and two-electron traps in this subset using HSE06 density functional theory calculations. Analysis of neutral precursor sites shows that trapping propensity is not determined by a universal O-Si-O angle or Si-O bond length; it is controlled by the accessibility of the relaxed trap geometry, requiring both local strain and medium-range network flexibility. Single electrons predominantly form edge-centred polarons on distorted SiO4 tetrahedra, with occupied states 3.1-4.3 eV below the conduction band minimum. Injection of a second electron drives stronger lattice relaxation, most commonly Si-O bond elongation leading to rupture, thereby forming threefold-coordinated-Si (Si3) bipolarons and, in some cases, Si-Si-bonded bipolaron configurations. The calculated bipolaron energy ranges are consistent with optical absorption features at 3.7, 4.7, and 6.4 eV associated with intrinsic electron localization.

candidates.abstract: Simulating microstructure evolution requires tracking many moving grain and phase boundaries coupled to thermodynamic and mechanical fields. We present Gaussian-projected kinetics (GPK), a sharp-interface framework in which every cell stores an integer grain or phase label. Near a boundary, a temporary Gaussian projection of the label map provides the interface normal and curvature and is then discarded. Capillarity, chemistry, stored energy, transport and elasticity move the boundaries through one topology-preserving update. Because the Gaussian measurement length is fixed in physical units, mesh refinement keeps a consistent capillary scale without a diffuse interface. GPK models grain growth, recrystallisation, multiphase evolution and elastic-coupled solidification in two and three dimensions. It is verified on analytical benchmarks and compared grain by grain with phase-field simulations, running 8.5 to 96 times faster at matched accuracy in our tests. An Al-Cu application with CALPHAD thermodynamic data connects it to measured recrystallisation and precipitation data.

candidates.abstract: Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) thin films deposited by ion beam sputtering (IBS) are essential components in high-power laser systems, where post-deposition annealing is routinely used to optimize film quality. In this work, we systematically investigate the structural and optical evolution of IBS-deposited Ta2O5 single layers subjected to post-deposition annealing at temperatures from 400 to 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The films undergo an amorphous-to-polycrystalline transition between 600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, accompanied by a marked increase in surface roughness. Argon bubbles inherently incorporated during IBS serve as structural markers: their size correlates positively with the surface roughness from the as-deposited to 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ but decouples at 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, revealing a transition from matrix-relaxation-dominated to surface-diffusion-dominated behavior. Transmittance spectra show a red shift at 400 and 600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ which can be explained by physical thickness increase. Weak absorption decreases from ~6 ppm in as-deposited films to ~2 ppm at 400-600 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ due to annihilation of oxygen vacancies, rises markedly at 700 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ due to grain-boundary defects and then drops again at 800 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as grain boundaries relax. We identify 400 $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as the optimal annealing window for IBS-deposited Ta2O5 single layers, with the lowest surface roughness and effectively reducing weak absorption while preserving the amorphous phase.

candidates.abstract: Optical zeros are momenta where the interband dipole vanishes. The dipole phase winds around each of them by an integer, so they are vortices of the resonant optical response with a conserved charge. We show that in rhombohedral graphene multilayers one integer, the stacking chirality $N$, fixes their constellation near the $K$ valley: the total charge per linear polarization is $N-1$ and is conserved under trigonal warping and interlayer bias; for $N\ge3$ the $K$ point stays an exact optical zero, the Bernal bilayer being the only exception; warping places the remaining charge on satellites whose radii scale linearly with the warping; and the charge pinned at $K$ is bias independent for $N\ge4$. A quantized interband character counts the enclosed charge as an integer staircase with steps at these radii, and an interlayer bias drives a satellite through the protected $K$ vortex in the trilayer. The rules survive the remote hoppings of the full tight-binding model and, being integer charges, the corrections that reshape the bands. The same integer sets the magnitude of the response: the band-edge shift current grows linearly with $N$.

candidates.abstract: The coherent elastic wave in untextured polycrystals, central to ultrasonic and seismic characterization, was recently observed to have two modes per polarization at short wavelengths. However, their physical origin and amplitude partition have remained open. We address both by theory, grain-scale numerical simulations and a grain velocity estimate. The first-order smoothing approximation, simplified by the far-field approximation, predicts three waves, which are the classical effective wave and one for each type of scattered wave (longitudinal and transverse). At long wavelengths, only the effective wave is weakly attenuated. At short wavelengths, one of the other two waves joins it with comparable attenuation, whereas the third stays far more attenuated. A new residue method, which needs no fitting, gives the same pattern for the amplitude partition, with the two waves sharing the coherent field and the third carrying little. The simulations reveal exactly these two modes, for transverse waves in iron and longitudinal waves in strongly anisotropic SrMgSn, and never the third. The wavefields reveal the mechanism, in which the incident wave is extinguished within one grain correlation length and the coherent field is rebuilt by forward multiple scattering. Strikingly, a grain velocity estimate from single-crystal constants provides independent evidence, tracing the two modes to plane waves of the individual grains and closely reproducing their velocities. Observability of multiple waves is thus set by attenuation and amplitude partition together, and short-wavelength measurements in random media must allow for more than one coherent mode.

candidates.abstract: Orthogonal metals provide a paradigmatic example of strongly entangled metallic states whose transport and thermodynamic properties resemble those of conventional Fermi liquids, while their single-electron excitations remain fundamentally distinct. Despite considerable interest in their unusual ground-state properties, orthogonal metals in three spatial dimensions and their finite-temperature behavior remain relatively unexplored. Here, we investigate a three-dimensional orthogonal metal and characterize the thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures associated with its finite-temperature phase transition. Starting from a simple model of fermions coupled to spin degrees of freedom, we perturbatively demonstrate that the thermal transition known to occur in the purely bosonic limit persists in the presence of coupling to a gapless Fermi surface. We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes. In particular, we calculate the evolution of the physical-electron spectral function and identify characteristic signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find a pronounced contrast in low-energy spectral weight between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes without requiring conventional symmetry-breaking order. Our results establish finite-temperature orthogonal-metal physics as a possible mechanism for pseudogap-like behavior in three-dimensional and quasi-two-dimensional layered materials with non-negligible interlayer hopping, which may be applied to the recent experiments in $\mathrm{Sr_2 VO_3 Fe As}$.

candidates.abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. STEM reveals an approximately 15 Ang separation, while EDX shows localized interfacial oxygen enrichment. After soft annealing, geometric phase analysis and plan-view TEM show a modified strain-relaxation pathway and strongly suppressed threading-dislocation emergence. Raman spectroscopy indicates a reduction in residual tensile strain from approximately 0.10 % to 0.05 %, whereas spreading resistance profiling confirms preservation of the Ge carrier profile. Current-confined electrochemistry therefore provides a controllable post-epitaxial route for buried-interface decoupling, defect filtering, and strain control in lattice-mismatched semiconductor heterostructures.

candidates.abstract: Monolayer FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (001) exemplifies interface-enhanced superconductivity, exhibiting a transition temperature nearly ten times that of bulk FeSe. Yet, its tunneling spectra lack clearly identifiable superconducting coherence peaks, preventing an unambiguous determination of the gap magnitude. Here, we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy as a function of temperature, tip-sample separation, and lateral position to disentangle tunneling contributions by statistical analysis. Decay rates extracted by regression of tip-height-dependent spectroscopy reveal three energy regimes: Andreev-reflection-dominated tunneling below 6 meV, mixed Andreev and quasiparticle tunneling between 6 and 13 meV, and predominantly quasiparticle tunneling above 13 meV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy and correlation analysis further reveal that the tunneling conductance is predominantly localized near defects below 6 meV but becomes spatially extended at higher energies. Together, these results constrain the superconducting gap to lie between 6 and 13 meV. Our findings establish statistical analysis of spectroscopy as a powerful approach to constraining superconducting gap structures when complex spectral features prevent the unambiguous identification of coherence peaks.
